blocks.text:
## Three South American countries in one journey

This 12-day programme brings together Brazil, Argentina and Chile. Spend your first 3 nights in Rio de Janeiro, then see Iguazu Falls from the Brazilian and Argentine sides, continue to Buenos Aires and finish in Santiago de Chile, with a trip to Valparaíso and Viña del Mar.

In Rio, the programme includes Corcovado, Christ the Redeemer and Sugarloaf. At Iguazu, the focus is on the waterfalls and tropical national parks. In Buenos Aires, enjoy a city tour and a tango show with dinner. In Chile, explore historic and modern Santiago before heading to the Pacific coast.

You can add excursions in Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires and Santiago: helicopter flights, hang gliding, the Macuco Safari, the Bird Park, a trip to Montevideo, Fiesta Gaucha, Tigre and the Maipo Valley wineries.

## Optional excursions in Rio de Janeiro

**Rio at night: Brazilian dance show**

USD 120 per person, or USD 100 per person for the show-only option.

Transfers are not included and can be arranged separately.

**Mysteries of Old Rio**

Private tour with an English-speaking guide, minimum 2 people.

The tour ends with coffee at the historic Confeitaria Colombo; food and drinks are paid for separately.

Price on request.

**Helicopter flight over Rio de Janeiro**

Options last approximately 6 or 13 minutes.

**Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden**

Private tour, minimum 2 people, with an English-speaking guide.

Price on request.

**Rio de Janeiro favela tour**

Choose a group tour with an English-speaking guide or a private tour with an English-speaking guide, minimum 2 people.

Group and private tour prices on request.

**Hang gliding in Rio de Janeiro**

Transfers and video recording are included.

Price on request.

## Optional excursions at Iguazu

**Rafain show and dinner**

Price on request.

Drinks are not included.

**Iguazu Bird Park**

Price on request.

**Helicopter flight over Iguazu Falls**

Duration approximately 10 minutes.

Price on request, minimum 3 people.

## Optional excursions in Buenos Aires

**Buenos Aires and Tigre tour**

Group tour with an English-speaking guide.

USD 100 per person.

**Montevideo, Uruguay: full-day trip**

Ferry tickets are included.

Prices for the group tour with an English-speaking guide and the private tour with an English-speaking guide, minimum 2 people, are available on request.

**Fiesta Gaucha ranch excursion**

Full-day group trip to a ranch.

USD 320 per person.

## Optional excursion in Santiago

**Maipo Valley winery tour**

Private tour with an English-speaking guide, minimum 2 people.

USD 290 per person.

## The route and experiences in each country

### Rio de Janeiro

Rio fills the first 3 days of this programme. Discover the city gradually: first the drive from the airport past green slopes and the ocean, then Corcovado, followed by Sugarloaf and the historic centre. This gives you views of Rio from above and from its streets.

At Corcovado, the train runs through Tijuca Forest. At the summit, the highlights are Christ the Redeemer and the city panorama. The next day, the Sugarloaf cable car gives you another perspective: Copacabana, Ipanema, Guanabara Bay, the Niterói Bridge, the islands and Corcovado share the view. After descending, continue through the central districts and their surviving colonial architecture.

Use your free time for the beach and walks on your own. Optional activities range from Old Rio and the Botanical Garden to a favela tour, a night-time show, a helicopter flight and hang gliding.

### Iguazu from both sides

Two days are devoted to the falls. The Brazilian side offers a broad panorama of the cascades. Paths follow the canyon and gradually bring you closer to the most powerful flows. On the Argentine side, the route runs among the water, with upper and lower circuits and a separate path to the Devil’s Throat.

The lower circuit lets you look up at the falling water. The upper circuit runs closer to the edge, where you can see the cascades begin their descent. The Devil’s Throat path ends at a platform beside the most powerful section of the falls. The routes vary in length and difficulty, so the full day on the Argentine side consists of several successive walks.

Optional activities around Iguazu add to your day. The Macuco Safari combines a forest journey with a motorboat ride near the falls. The Bird Park focuses on tropical species, while a short helicopter flight gives you an aerial view. In the evening, you can choose the Rafain show with dinner.

### Buenos Aires

After Iguazu, the journey moves from nature to a large city. The city tour introduces La Boca, San Telmo, Plaza Dorrego, Plaza de Mayo and the Casa Rosada. A tango show with dinner fills the evening of your first full day in the capital.

The following day is free, with 3 main optional trips. The first explores Tigre and the northern suburbs of Buenos Aires, with a boat trip through the delta. The second is a day trip by ferry to Montevideo. The third is Fiesta Gaucha at a ranch, with horse riding, asado, a folk show and displays of horsemanship.

Fiesta Gaucha follows a detailed schedule. At 11:00, guests are welcomed with empanadas and wine, followed by free time for walks and horse riding. Lunch begins at 13:00, with Argentine barbecue, drinks and dessert. A folk programme with tango follows, and at 15:00 the gauchos demonstrate their riding skills. Return to the city is scheduled for 16:30.

### Santiago, Valparaíso and Viña del Mar

Chile is the final country on the journey. In Santiago, the tour combines the historic centre with modern districts. The route takes in La Moneda and Plaza de Armas, climbs Santa Lucía Hill and continues through Vitacura, Las Condes and Providencia.

The next day is devoted to the coast. The road to Valparaíso crosses wine-growing valleys. The city itself spreads across hills connected by historic funiculars. After touring Valparaíso, continue to Viña del Mar, with its parks, promenades and beaches.

For a closer look at Chilean wine, you can add a private trip to the Maipo Valley, visiting wineries, learning about production and tasting wines.

## Main programme arrangements

Domestic flights between Rio de Janeiro, Iguazu, Buenos Aires and Santiago are included in the main price. Main excursions operate in groups with English-speaking guides, including the Valparaíso trip. Transfers are also shared.

Optional excursions are charged separately. Some have 2 prices for the same service; both prices are retained.
